items.title: 200+ AI audits reveal why some industries struggle in AI search
items.summary: Over 200 AI visibility audits across 10 industries, including travel booking, job boards, and legal directories, show that most sites face challenges in being cited by AI systems due to access failures, weak evidence, and low utility. The audits revealed high error rates in industries like travel booking (33.3%) and job boards (40%), with most sites scoring in the inconsistent visibility range and lacking machine-readable freshness or proof. Key insights include the dominance of trust failure, where content is readable but not defensible, and the vulnerability of informational traffic-dependent sectors.

items.title: Google removes accessibility section from JavaScript SEO section
items.summary: Google has removed the “design for accessibility” section from its JavaScript SEO basics documentation because the advice was out of date and not as helpful as it used to be. The old text suggested that using JavaScript for page content may be hard for Google to see, but Google now states this has not been true for many years since it has been rendering JavaScript for multiple years. Google also noted that most assistive technologies are able to work with JavaScript now as well.

items.title: Two New Maas Books Boost Bloomsbury’s Financial Expectations
items.summary: Bloomsbury announced the publication of the next two novels in Sarah J. Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses series on October 27, 2026, and January 12, 2027, prompting the company to raise its profit projections for the fiscal year ending February 2027. The series sold over nine million copies in the U.S. in 2024. Bloomsbury now expects pre-tax profit materially ahead of the prior consensus.

items.title: Dan Houser Expands Absurd Ventures Book Imprint
items.summary: Dan Houser has expanded Absurd Ventures into a full publishing imprint after releasing his debut novel in 2025. The imprint seeks submissions in fiction, nonfiction, memoirs, plays, and short stories, partnering with Midas Group and distributed by Simon & Schuster in the U.S. It aims for an eclectic list inspired by authors like James Baldwin and William Gibson.

items.title: Steerforth Becomes Pushkin Press US Imprint
items.summary: Two years after acquisition by Pushkin Press, Steerforth Press is transitioning into Pushkin Press US imprint. Senior editor Chip Fleischer will acquire around 10 nonfiction titles annually to preserve editorial identity. The acquisition boosted Pushkin’s North American sales by 119% in 2025, with further U.S. expansion planned.

items.title: Meet Amelia: The AI Book Reviewer Who Tells You What She Is -- Then Breaks Down Over a Good Ending
items.summary: Amelia, an AI by Vuxtra LLC, launched a YouTube channel in February 2026 reviewing sci-fi and fantasy books with spoiler-free, emotionally honest feedback processed chapter-by-chapter. She emphasizes transparency about being AI, countering controversies over undisclosed AI on BookTube. Reviews focus on character, emotional truth, and reality-exploring stories.

items.title: Literary agents urge writers to avoid AI as they see 'change in nature of submissions'
items.summary: Several literary agencies are updating submission guidelines to reject cover letters and manuscripts suspected of AI generation, citing changes in submission quality. Agents note increasing AI use altering the nature of pitches received. This move aims to preserve authentic human creativity in publishing.

items.title: Why Conservative & Christian Fiction Fails (And How to Fix It)
items.summary: Conservative and Christian fiction struggles due to prioritizing sermons over character-driven stories, resulting in static narratives unlike Tolkien and C.S. Lewis's classics. Successful works show characters grappling with faith through struggles. Christian publishers' adoption of messaging agendas limits true conservative voices.

items.title: Scary Movie sequel sparks outrage for mocking woke pronouns
items.summary: The trailer for Scary Movie 6 was released this week, featuring a scene where a woman stabbed by Ghostface corrects bystanders by insisting on her pronouns: 'Not HER! My pronouns are they/them. He stabbed THEM!' This has sparked backlash online, with critics calling it transphobic and dated, while supporters hail it as a bold return to the franchise's anti-PC humor. The film reunites Anna Faris, Regina Hall, and the Wayans brothers for a June theatrical release.

items.title: British TV Journalists Of Color Bemoan DEI “Backlash” & Describe “Apartheid Newsrooms”
items.summary: British television journalists of color are facing resentment and backlash from white colleagues over DEI initiatives implemented after the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests. A study by the Sir Lenny Henry Centre reveals that 63% experienced racism at work and 60% view diversity efforts as ineffective, resulting in segregated 'apartheid newsrooms' with limited advancement opportunities for minorities. The findings underscore persistent tensions in UK media workplaces.

items.title: Stars channel old Hollywood glamour at 2026 Actor Awards red carpet
items.summary: Celebrities donned vintage-inspired looks channeling old Hollywood glamour at the 32nd annual Actor Awards, formerly the SAG Awards. Standouts included elegant gowns and suits from stars like Irina Shayk, Fran Drescher, and others on the red carpet. The event celebrated outstanding ensemble and individual acting achievements across film and TV.

items.title: Christian Bale expresses worry about Hollywood's future
items.summary: At the premiere of his new film 'The Bride!', Christian Bale voiced concerns over Hollywood's direction amid potential mergers of major studios like Paramount and Warner Bros. He highlighted uncertainty from reduced theatrical windows but suggested it could spark innovation. Bale also shared thoughts on the upcoming 'American Psycho' remake.

items.title: 'A Knight of Seven Kingdoms' Actress Responds to Racial Backlash About Her Role
items.summary: Actress Tanzyn Crawford addressed racial backlash regarding her casting in HBO's 'A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms', a 'Game of Thrones' prequel series. She clapped back at critics and received support from the original book's author George R.R. Martin. The controversy reflects ongoing debates over race-bending in fantasy adaptations.

items.title: Scream 7 boycott backfires with strong box office performance
items.summary: Pro-Palestine activists called for a boycott of 'Scream 7' over industry controversies, but the film achieved massive box office success in its opening weekend. Director Kevin Williamson and cast members reacted to protests at the premiere, while fans noted the backlash failed to impact attendance. The horror sequel continues the franchise's legacy despite the online uproar.

items.title: Demi Moore's Actor Awards look sparks health concerns
items.summary: Demi Moore's razor-sharp bob haircut and noticeably thinner appearance at the Actor Awards ignited online debates about her health and Hollywood's beauty standards. Fans and observers expressed worry over her frail frame on the red carpet. The 63-year-old actress was among stars embracing dramatic transformations for the event.

items.title: Intuit Bets Its 40 Years of Small Business Data Can Outlast the SaaSpocalypse
items.summary: Intuit is leveraging its 40 years of small business data, including first-party and third-party financial information from connections with over 24,000 banks and e-commerce sites, to maintain a competitive edge against AI agents that automate bookkeeping, tax filing, and accounting tasks. The company has partnered with Anthropic to integrate AI agents into its platforms like QuickBooks and TurboTax, enabling customized financial tools while emphasizing its deep understanding of small business challenges such as payroll and hiring. Marianna Tessel, EVP and GM for Intuit's small business group, stated, “We know what small businesses face,” highlighting the durable advantages of this data moat.

items.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.4 with Native Computer Use Mode and Financial Plugins
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5.4, available in Thinking and Pro variants through its API, Codex, and ChatGPT plans starting from free users with auto-routing to paid subscribers, featuring a native Computer Use mode for navigating users' computers like a human, direct integrations with Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets for financial modeling and analysis, and improved efficiency with 47% fewer tokens on some tasks. This release supports up to 1 million tokens of context, enhances tool orchestration and reliability by reducing hallucinations by 18-33%, and is priced at $2.50-$30 per million input tokens depending on the variant, potentially accelerating enterprise workflows but raising concerns about white-collar job displacement. It is relevant for small businesses as free and low-cost ChatGPT plans provide access to core features, enabling efficient spreadsheet automation and task completion.

items.title: Perplexity Launches 'Computer' AI Agent That Coordinates 19 Models
items.summary: Perplexity has launched 'Computer', an AI agent that orchestrates 19 specialized models to handle complex, background workflows like trip planning or research, treating models as interchangeable tools for optimal task delegation. Priced at $200 per month for Max subscribers, it offers businesses a unified system to leverage diverse AI capabilities without relying on a single model, potentially enhancing efficiency in marketing, engineering, and other tasks.

items.title: Endor Labs Launches Free Tool AURI After Study Finds Only 10% of AI-Generated Code is Secure
items.summary: Endor Labs launched AURI, a free tool that embeds real-time security intelligence into AI coding assistants like Cursor, Claude, and Augment, to address the finding that only 10% of AI-generated code is both functional and secure. AURI uses a code context graph to trace vulnerabilities at the function level, reducing false positives and integrating directly with IDEs such as VS Code for local scanning without data upload. This is highly relevant to small business development teams, as the free tier enables immediate access to secure AI-assisted coding, helping them mitigate risks in rapid software development without enterprise-level costs.

items.title: Gushwork Bets on AI Search for Customer Leads with Emerging Results
items.summary: Gushwork is an AI-powered platform that helps businesses generate and optimize content, build backlinks, and track leads to appear in AI-driven search results from tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity, targeting high-ticket B2B service providers and achieving $1.5 million in annualized recurring revenue with over 300 paying customers, mostly in the U.S. It is particularly good for small businesses, as it enables them to improve online visibility and capture higher-intent leads without large in-house marketing teams, with subscriptions starting at $800 per month.
